RANKIN COUNTY – A 14-year-old juvenile detainee was captured Thursday night after escaping from the Rankin County Juvenile Detention Center and later leading deputies on a pursuit in a stolen vehicle.

According to the Rankin County Sheriff’s Office, officers at the detention center reported around 3 p.m. May 21 that a juvenile detainee had escaped from the facility in Pelahatchie after climbing a security fence and running away.

Sheriff Bryan Bailey said detainees were participating in mandatory outdoor recreation, with several playing basketball, when the basketball rolled near the perimeter fence. The juvenile ran toward the ball and began climbing the 16-foot security fence.

A detention officer responded and grabbed the juvenile while he was on the fence, attempting to pull him back down. The sheriff’s office said the juvenile broke free, climbed over the fence and ran into a wooded area.

Deputies and assisting law enforcement agencies responded and established a perimeter. Rankin County Sheriff’s Office K-9 units, Flowood Police Department K-9 units, Mississippi Highway Patrol K-9 units and the sheriff’s office drone team assisted in the search.

Authorities said an extensive ground and aerial search continued through the afternoon and evening, and checkpoints were set up in the surrounding area.

Around 11 p.m., a Banks Street resident called 911 and reported that the escapee was at her home attempting to steal her husband’s white Chevrolet 2500 pickup truck. The caller said the juvenile left the residence traveling west on Highway 80 toward Brandon.

Deputies soon located the stolen vehicle and attempted a traffic stop, but the juvenile refused to stop, leading deputies on a pursuit that lasted about 20 minutes and traveled along several county roads.

Deputies attempted to direct the pursuit toward Brandon, where Brandon police had deployed stop sticks. The juvenile eventually turned onto Mount Ridge Road, a dead-end road, where deputies were able to box in the vehicle.

Authorities said the juvenile then attempted to escape through a cutover area but became stuck. Deputies reached the vehicle and took him into custody before he could run away again.

Pafford Ambulance Service responded and transported the juvenile to a local hospital for treatment of injuries sustained during the escape. After treatment, he was returned to the custody of the Rankin County Juvenile Detention Center.

The sheriff’s office said the stolen vehicle sustained heavy damage. The owner operates a small landscaping business and relies on the truck for work.

The juvenile was originally being held at the detention center on charges of auto theft and auto burglary. He is scheduled to appear before Youth Court Judge Josh McCrory.

The Rankin County Juvenile Detention Center opened in 2011, and officials said this was the first escape in the facility’s history. Bailey and McCrory are reevaluating outdoor recreation security procedures and plan to implement additional measures while staying in compliance with state and federal guidelines for juvenile detention facilities.

Bailey thanked deputies, dispatchers, detention officers and assisting agencies, including the Mississippi Highway Patrol, Pelahatchie Police Department, Flowood Police Department, Brandon Police Department, Madison Police Department and Scott County Sheriff’s Department.

“We hope the quick recapture of this escapee provides peace of mind to our citizens,” Bailey said.

CHOCTAW – Tribal community ponds have been restocked with catfish just in time for Memorial Day weekend, the Mississippi Band of Choctaw Indians announced.

The restocking was announced by Tribal Chief Cyrus Ben and includes ponds in several tribal communities.

The stocked ponds include Pearl River Community Pond, Town Center Pond in Pearl River, the pond in front of Lake Pushmataha in Pearl River, Fani Lakna Pond in Tucker, Tucker Community Pond and Bogue Chitto Community Pond in Neshoba County.

Other stocked locations include Conehatta Community Pond in Newton County; Standing Pine Community Pond, Standing Pine School Pond and Attala Pond in Leake County; and Crystal Ridge Pond in Winston County.

Community members are invited to bring family and friends out for fishing, fellowship and outdoor fun during the holiday weekend.

Officials are reminding anglers to practice a courtesy limit of five catfish per person and to be mindful of others.

LAWRENCE COUNTY -vThe Lawrence County Sheriff’s Office is urging residents to secure their homes and vehicles after several burglaries were reported over the past week.

Sheriff Ryan Everett said the county had gone a long time without a residential or vehicle burglary, but deputies have recently investigated one residential burglary, one attempted residential burglary and two automobile burglaries.

Everett encouraged residents to lock their homes and vehicles and avoid leaving valuables in plain sight. He also reminded people to keep records of important property, including brands, model numbers, calibers and serial numbers, so items can be more easily identified if stolen.

The sheriff also urged residents to practice firearm safety, including treating every gun as if it is loaded.

Everett warned those committing burglaries that there would be no sympathy from his office and encouraged them to change course before facing serious consequences.

The sheriff’s office is asking residents to remain alert and take steps to protect their property.

LEAKE COUNTY – A large amount of drugs and several firearms were seized during a drug bust in Leake County, according to the Leake County Sheriff’s Office.

Sheriff Randy W. Atkinson said deputies and investigators seized 395 grams of methamphetamine, 54 grams of spice, 10 grams of marijuana and five firearms from a home off Pearl Hill Road.

According to the sheriff’s office, the methamphetamine seized was 58 grams shy of a pound and had an estimated street value of $5,000.

One person was taken into custody during the operation. The sheriff’s office did not immediately release the person’s name or charges.

No injuries were reported during the arrest, and officials said public safety remained the top priority throughout the operation.

The sheriff’s office is encouraging anyone with information about drug activity to contact deputies.

RANKIN COUNTY — A Rankin County Sheriff’s Office K-9 deputy has been medically retired after collapsing during a search Thursday afternoon for an escaped juvenile offender in Pelahatchie.

According to the Rankin County Sheriff’s Office, Deputy Ronnie Decell and his K-9 partner, Fox, responded May 21 to assist in locating a juvenile who had escaped from the Rankin County Juvenile Detention Center.

Officials said Deputy Decell deployed Fox to track the suspect, but about 100 yards into the search, the dog suddenly collapsed.

Deputy Decell carried Fox back to his patrol vehicle and rushed him to the after-hours emergency veterinary clinic URGIVET in Madison for treatment.

Veterinarians later determined Fox was suffering from an undiagnosed tumor that ruptured during the track, causing severe internal bleeding near his heart, according to the sheriff’s office.

Fox remains under treatment and observation for what officials described as a life-threatening condition. Because of the diagnosis, the sheriff’s office said Fox will be medically retired from service.

Fox, a 10-year-old Belgian Malinois, is trained and certified in narcotics detection, tracking and handler protection. The sheriff’s office said he has served Rankin County throughout his career alongside Deputy Decell.

Sheriff Bryan Bailey asked the community to keep Deputy Decell, his family and Fox in their thoughts and prayers.

TUPELO – A Tupelo man was arrested after police said he was connected to fraudulent check reports at two BNA Bank locations.

According to the Tupelo Police Department, officers responded May 19 to BNA Bank at 2919 Tom Watson Drive after employees reported that a suspect had cashed a check that was later determined to be fraudulent.

A short time later, officers responded to another BNA Bank at 3041 McCullough Blvd. after employees reported that a suspect had attempted to cash a fraudulent check and left the scene.

Police said employees were able to provide a description of the suspect, which matched the description from the earlier report.

Later that day, patrol officers found a person matching the suspect’s description. The person was arrested on unrelated misdemeanor charges.

After further investigation, 44-year-old Samuel T. Dickson, of Tupelo, was charged May 21 with two counts of false pretense.

Tupelo Municipal Court Judge Weir ordered Dickson held on a $10,000 bond.

The charges will be presented to the Lee County grand jury.

TUPELO – The Tupelo Police Department is warning parents and guardians after receiving complaints about toy guns being used in neighborhoods.

Police said the complaints involve “Orby guns,” gel blasters, splatter guns and similar toy guns.

According to the department, many of the toys can look realistic and may be mistaken for real firearms, especially from a distance or at night.

Police are asking parents and guardians to talk with children about using the toys responsibly and not pointing or shooting them at strangers, passing vehicles, homes or anyone who may not know they are toys.

The department said situations involving realistic-looking guns can quickly create dangerous misunderstandings for residents and responding law enforcement officers.

Police said they appreciate the public’s help in keeping these situations from escalating into something more serious.

ABERDEEN — Two Louisville men have been sentenced in federal court after pleading guilty to drug trafficking charges involving methamphetamine, cocaine, fentanyl and heroin, according to federal officials.

Aaron Hughes, 33, was sentenced March 24 to 108 months in federal prison followed by three years of supervised release. Hughes also was convicted on a firearms charge.

Warren Goss, 58, was sentenced May 12 to 70 months in federal prison followed by three years of supervised release.

Both men previously pleaded guilty to possession with intent to distribute methamphetamine, cocaine, fentanyl, despropionyl fentanyl and heroin. Senior U.S. District Judge Sharion Aycock handed down the sentences.

Federal officials said the convictions stemmed from a Homeland Security Task Force operation involving the Federal Bureau of Investigation, Homeland Security Investigations and the Louisville Police Department.

U.S. Attorney Scott Leary said authorities have “zero tolerance” for fentanyl, methamphetamine, cocaine, heroin and illegal firearms.

FBI Special Agent in Charge Robert Eikhoff said the sentences should serve as a warning to others involved in violent crime and drug trafficking.

The case was prosecuted as part of the Homeland Security Task Force initiative, a multiagency effort targeting criminal organizations and drug trafficking operations.

Assistant U.S. Attorneys Sam Stringfellow and Julie Addison prosecuted the case.

VICKSBURG – The Vicksburg Police Department is clarifying details about a medical call involving the person accused in a robbery at Tommy’s BBQ after receiving multiple calls from the public.

Police said concerns had been raised about whether the individual was in Vicksburg police custody earlier the same day before the robbery.

According to VPD, 911 dispatch received a call around 6 p.m. Saturday, May 16, requesting a mental or medical evaluation for an individual reportedly exhibiting unusual behavior, including talking to stop signs and sweating heavily.

Fire Medic 30, Engine 6 and a Vicksburg police officer were dispatched to the scene. Police said the officer responded to provide routine scene security and standby support because of the nature of the call.

According to a review of 911 calls, radio traffic and related records, the individual was not reported to be a threat to himself or others and was not reported to have any weapons.

Police said the responding officer made routine contact with the individual and asked standard questions related to the medical call and the person’s well-being. Once the individual entered the ambulance, police said he remained calm and did not exhibit disruptive behavior.

The officer then cleared the scene and returned to service without incident.

The individual was taken by Fire Medic 30 to Merit Health River Region without incident. Police said that, based on the information reviewed, the individual became disruptive after arriving at the hospital, and EMS requested assistance from sheriff’s deputies.

VPD said the individual was not in the custody of the Vicksburg Police Department before the robbery and did not show disruptive or uncooperative behavior that would have warranted detention during the initial medical call.

The department said the clarification was released to provide transparency and address community concerns about the timeline of events.

OXFORD — A Booneville man was sentenced to four years in federal prison after investigators found thousands of files containing child sexual abuse material, according to federal authorities.

Joshua Honeycutt, 42, was sentenced May 21 by U.S. District Judge Michael Mills to 48 months in prison, followed by 10 years of supervised release. He will also be required to register as a sex offender and pay $107,000 in restitution to victims.

According to court documents, Honeycutt possessed more than 4,000 videos and 17,000 images depicting children under 12 engaged in sexually explicit conduct. Authorities said many of the victims shown were between 5 and 10 years old.

The case was investigated by the Federal Bureau of Investigation, the Mississippi Attorney General’s Office, and the Prentiss County Sheriff’s Department.

U.S. Attorney Scott Leary said the sentence removes a dangerous offender from the public and emphasized the importance of restitution for victims. FBI Jackson Special Agent in Charge Robert Eikhoff said the agency remains committed to combating child exploitation and protecting children from abuse.

Attorney General Lynn Fitch called child sexual abuse “a horrific crime” that causes lasting trauma for victims, especially when images or videos continue to circulate.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Parker S. King prosecuted the case as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative aimed at combating online child exploitation.

BILOXI — A man died early Sunday morning after a violent encounter at a home in the Woolmarket area of Biloxi during severe flooding conditions, according to police.

Authorities said that around 8 p.m. Saturday, May 23, Biloxi Police Department dispatchers received a 911 call from the 11000 block of Woolmarket Lake Road. The caller reported that they were away from home but had seen a naked white male emerge from the Biloxi River on their Ring doorbell camera, walk up the stairs of the residence, and enter the porch area.

Dispatchers also reportedly received multiple calls from the surrounding area about a naked man.

Police said the homeowner contacted a next-door neighbor and asked them to check on the property. The neighbor approached the home and spoke with the man on the porch, asking whether he needed help.

According to investigators, the man suddenly charged the neighbor and struck him. The neighbor then fired multiple shots, hitting the man, but police said the man continued attacking him. During the struggle, the man reportedly disarmed the neighbor and then walked away from the residence and back into the floodwaters.

Emergency crews faced difficulty reaching the area because of heavy flooding, and officers had to be transported by boat.

When officers arrived, they found the neighbor suffering from facial lacerations and bruising. Investigators also reviewed the home’s security footage, which police said captured the entire incident.

A search operation was conducted by rescue boat, and at approximately 2 a.m. Sunday, May 24, authorities located the man’s body on shore near where the incident occurred.

The identity of the deceased has not yet been released.
